text:
maria: Quick sync — I'm drafting a geo resilience playbook focused on multi-region behavior + tenant isolation. Goal: crisp launch criteria, a small policy DSL, canary/runbook steps, and an explicit prioritization for customer-driven asks. Thoughts?

aj: Love it. Can we ground this in 3 canonical customer scenarios: 1) PLG high-throughput app, 2) enterprise with strict data residency, 3) regulated on-prem customer? That makes tradeoffs easier.

sunil: Architecturally I want the playbook to mandate a precedence model: tenant-level policy > region-affinity > capacity-fallback. Also propose we define "soft quarantine" (traffic throttled + telemetry) vs "hard eviction" (immediate routing out).

taylor: Ops needs: explicit runbooks for surge, cross-region failover, and manual tenant eviction. Telemetry triggers we can use: 95th latency, error-rate windows, retriable errors percentage. We'll add exact thresholds in the SLO doc.

olivia: From sales: customers will ask for a clear SLA and an isolation pricing line item. They'll ask how long failover takes and whether KV cache is preserved — we need language for expectations.

maria: Draft launch criteria proposal: 1) policy DSL v1 implemented and tested, 2) canary (2 customers across regions) passing for 48h, 3) automated fallback path to compatible model variant, 4) runbook + SLO dashboards in Console, 5) pricing appendix for isolation. Agree?

aj: Prioritization suggestion: score by customer impact (40%), risk reduction (30%), implementation effort (30%). With that, policy DSL + telemetry + fallback rank highest.

sunil: Minimal DSL sample to include in spec so everyone talks the same language: 
```policy
route: {
  match: { region: "eu", tenant: "T123" }
  action: { isolate: true, fallback: "us-west", cache: "prefix-preserve" }
}
```
We should also call out versioning, migration semantics, and what constitutes a compatible fallback (model arch + quantization bounds).

taylor: Ops playbook fragment idea: 
- detect -> notify customer -> shift traffic to fallback lane -> preserve/flush KV cache according to policy -> monitor health -> if degradation persists, escalate to manual eviction.
Make sure the Console shows a one-click rollback.

olivia: Also document sales-facing FAQs: "How long to cutover?" "Is data ever routed outside requested region?" "Pricing for isolation per-month". We can put sample contract language.

maria: Plan: I'll assemble a PRD with sections: overview, policy DSL, telemetry & SLOs, runbooks, canary plan, launch criteria, pricing appendix. @aj please estimate implementation effort; @sunil write DSL compatibility notes; @taylor draft runbook skeleton. Target: PRD draft by EOD next Tue.
deploy-bot: Reminder scheduled: PRD draft due 2024-05-07 09:00 UTC.
aj: I'll do a first-pass on estimates by EOD tomorrow.
sunil: Will add backward-compatibility notes and a short matrix of supported model variants for fallback.
taylor: I'll sketch the runbook tonight and post a strawman.
maria: Thanks — once I post the PRD I'll ping folks for a short review window (48h).
